name: openjev
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B: 8 full GQA layers (kv heads 4, head_dim 256) and 24 other layers, per the base config.json.
notes: ADDED 2026-10-25. A finetune of Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, not a new base model: same config.json, same 4.66 parameters (identical tensor set). Recorded as a contender because it publishes benchmark evidence against its own base; the evidence rows below are card-sourced and marked vendor_claim. Licence mit, repo created 2026-09-16. CLASSIFIED, NOT REJECTED: task=decision. openjev is Qwen3.5-4B retrained as a cross-encoder entailment scorer; you hand it a state and a closed set of options and get one probability per option from the model's own softmax, with no text generated. Chat benchmarks therefore say nothing about it and it is excluded from the worth-running ranking by construction. Evidence read from the card: JevBench v1.2 public 231 items — 4B v5 0.814 vs the plain Qwen3.5-4B 'SemIf' column 0.810, so the margin over its own base is 0.4 points; hard tier 0.622 vs 0.613; standard tier 0.986 vs 0.986 (a tie). It LOSES outright to Jev 1.13 (0.866 public, 0.730 hard). The card reports no Decision Index 0.2.1 score, so nothing was added to data/decision_index.jsonl. Card-stated weaknesses kept as-is: shell-command safety 0.600 acc / 37% of deny-worthy caught, and prompt injection drops JevBench accuracy 0.833 -> 0.467. The v5 checkpoint deliberately trains on MMLU/ARC/GSM8K/GPQA-diamond/CLINC/Banking77/ESCI TEST splits, so no numbers from those benchmarks are recordable. Order invariance was measured on the card (0/231 label changes under shuffle).
